Documents.Title: Patient Registration SOP
Documents.Content:
# Patient Registration Standard Operating Procedure

## Purpose
To ensure accurate and consistent patient registration across all HIS modules.

## Scope
Applies to all front-desk and administrative staff with access to the Patient Registration module.

## Procedure

### 1. Verify Patient Identity
- Request a valid government-issued photo ID.
- Cross-reference against existing records using the **Patient Search** function.
- If a duplicate is found, merge records using the Duplicate Resolution workflow.

### 2. Capture Demographic Data
Collect the following mandatory fields:
- Full legal name (First, Middle, Last)
- Date of birth
- National ID / Passport number
- Contact number and emergency contact
- Medical aid scheme and membership number (if applicable)

### 3. Assign Encounter Number
The system auto-generates a unique Encounter Number upon saving. Print and attach the wristband before the patient proceeds to triage.

### 4. Sync to PHENICS
Patient records are automatically pushed to the **PHENICS Master** via the *Patient Admissions Sync* flow within 2 minutes of saving.

> **Note:** If the PHENICS sync indicator shows a warning, do not re-register the patient. Log an incident via the Forms page instead.

## References
- PHENICS Module 3 Guide
- Data Privacy Guidelines

Documents.Title: PHENICS Module 3 Integration Guide
Documents.Content:
# PHENICS Module 3 — HIS Integration Guide

## Overview
Module 3 governs the bidirectional exchange of clinical encounter data between the local HIS database and the PHENICS Master aggregation system.

## Architecture

```
HIS Local DB  ←──────────────────→  PHENICS Master
  (MSSQL)         Patient Admissions      (Remote)
                  Sync (Bidirectional)
```

## Endpoints

| Flow | Source | Destination | Frequency |
|------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| Patient Admissions | HIS Local DB | PHENICS Master | Real-time |
| Lab Results Export | LIS Module | PHENICS Lab Endpoint | Every 5 min |
| Billing Data Rollup | Finance Module | PHENICS Finance | Hourly |
| Pharmacy Inventory | Pharmacy DB | PHENICS Logistics | Every 10 min |

## Troubleshooting

### Flow shows "Warning" status
1. Navigate to the **Flows** page in HIS Data Hub.
2. Click **View Logs** on the affected flow.
3. Identify the last successful sync timestamp.
4. If gap > 1 hour, trigger a manual re-sync via the **Sync** button.
5. If re-sync fails, submit an **Incident Report** form.

### PHENICS API returns 401
The service account token may have expired. Contact the PHENICS system administrator to rotate the service credentials.

## Configuration
All sync intervals and retry logic are managed by the PHENICS scheduler. Contact the integration team to adjust thresholds.

Documents.Title: Data Privacy and Handling Policy
Documents.Content:
# Data Privacy and Handling Policy

## 1. Purpose
To define the organisation's obligations regarding the collection, storage, processing, and sharing of patient health data in compliance with applicable legislation.

## 2. Scope
All staff, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to HIS systems or patient data.

## 3. Principles

### 3.1 Data Minimisation
Collect only the data necessary for the stated clinical or administrative purpose.

### 3.2 Purpose Limitation
Data collected for patient care may not be repurposed for marketing, research, or third-party sharing without explicit written consent.

### 3.3 Access Control
- All access is role-based.
- Data Access Requests must be submitted via the **Activity Forms** page.
- Access logs are retained for a minimum of **3 years**.

### 3.4 Data Retention
| Data Type | Retention Period |
|-----------|-----------------|
| Clinical records | 10 years post last encounter |
| Administrative logs | 3 years |
| Audit trails | 5 years |

## 4. Breach Response
In the event of a suspected data breach:
1. Immediately report to the Data Protection Officer (DPO).
2. Submit an **Incident Report** via the Forms page.
3. Do not attempt to contain the breach independently.

## 5. Third-Party Integrations
Vendors (including PHENICS and TIXO) are contractually bound by a Data Processing Agreement (DPA). Review current DPAs with the DPO annually.

Documents.Title: Data Access Request Guide
Documents.Content:
# Data Access Request — Submission Guide

## When to Use This Form
Submit a **Data Access Request** whenever you need access to:
- A PHENICS module you are not currently provisioned for.
- A restricted data warehouse or reporting schema.
- Patient records outside your assigned ward or department.

## How to Submit
1. Navigate to **Forms** in the top navigation bar.
2. Select **Data Access Request**.
3. Fill in the **Ticket Title** with a brief description: e.g., *"Access to PHENICS Finance Module — Billing Audit Q2"*.
4. Set **Priority** to:
   - **Low** — convenience / reporting access
   - **Medium** — operational requirement
   - **High** — clinical urgency
   - **Critical** — active patient safety concern
5. In the **Detailed Description**, include:
   - The specific module or dataset required.
   - The business justification.
   - The proposed access duration.
6. Click **Submit Ticket**. A TIXO reference number will be returned on success.

## Approval Turnaround
| Priority | Target Response |
|----------|----------------|
| Low | 5 business days |
| Medium | 2 business days |
| High | Same business day |
| Critical | Within 2 hours |

Part One
Hospital Deliveries — System Data Flow
Complete end-to-end workflow from pregnancy detection to postnatal care
01
System Overview
Purpose and scope of the Hospital Deliveries module within PHENICS

PHENICS (Primary Health Care Electronic Network Information and Communication System) is Lebanon's National Health Information System, designed to coordinate and digitize the continuum of care delivered across Primary Health Care Centers (PHCCs) and partner hospitals. The Hospital Deliveries module governs the end-to-end management of pregnant women from pregnancy registration through delivery and postnatal care.

This documentation describes the complete data flow for the hospital deliveries service program — covering pregnancy package activation, antenatal care (ANC) visit management, eligibility assessment, inter-facility referral, hospital-level activation, delivery recording, and discharge — and is intended for PHCC staff, PUI midwives, HFOs, and hospital administrators operating within PHENICS.

ℹ
Scope of this document
This document covers the operational flow for hospital deliveries and the associated file-checking procedures for the Health Field Officer (HFO). PNC services delivered at the PHCC after discharge are referenced but not separately detailed.
02
Overall Data Flow
End-to-end journey across three primary actors — PHCC, PUI Midwife, and Hospital

The workflow spans three primary actors coordinated through PHENICS. The flow is strictly sequential — each stage is a prerequisite for the next.

Stage 1 · PHCC

Pregnancy Detection & Package Activation

When pregnancy is confirmed, the Pregnancy Package is activated in PHENICS. Gestational age (number of pregnancy weeks) is a mandatory field — the package cannot be activated without it.

Pregnancy Package Gestational age — mandatory
Stage 2 · PHCC

ANC Visits — Auto-Approval Schedule

The pregnant woman attends ANC visits at the PHCC per the restriction manual for auto-approval. A minimum of 4 ANC visits must be completed before the patient is initially eligible for the delivery service program pool.

Minimum 4 ANC visits Auto-approval rules apply
Stage 3 · PHCC Midwife

Medical Assessment — Eligibility Criteria

During ANC visits, the PHCC midwife fills specific medical assessment sections of the eligibility criteria — clinical risk factors, pregnancy health status, and obstetric history indicators.

Medical sections PHCC midwife responsibility
Stage 4 · PUI Midwife

Socio-Economic Assessment — Eligibility Criteria

After the PHCC midwife completes the medical sections, the PUI midwife fills the socio-economic section — capturing household vulnerability and financial indicators forming part of the composite eligibility score.

Socio-economic section PUI midwife responsibility
Stage 5 · System

Eligibility Score Calculation

PHENICS calculates the composite eligibility score from both sections. The patient must achieve a score of ≥ 21 to be eligible for the delivery program. Patients below this threshold are not referred.

Score ≥ 21 → Eligible Score < 21 → Not referred
Stage 6 · PHCC → Hospital

Referral Initiation — Delivery Request Act

If the score is positive, the PHCC initiates a referral through the Delivery Request Act in PHENICS. The referral form is printed and handed to the pregnant woman to carry to the hospital.

Delivery Request Act Printed referral form
Stage 7 · Hospital

Hospital Activation — Referral & Patient IDs

The pregnant woman presents the referral form at the hospital. Staff extract two critical identifiers — the Referral ID and Patient ID — and use these to activate both the referral and the patient profile in PHENICS.

Referral ID Patient ID Hospital activation
Stage 8 · Hospital

Delivery Recording & Discharge Report Upload

Delivery details are recorded in PHENICS by the hospital. Upon completion, the hospital uploads the discharge report, closing the hospital episode and triggering the transition back to primary care.

Delivery recorded Discharge report uploaded
Stage 9 · PHCC

PNC Services — Patient Return to PHCC

Following discharge, the patient is directed back to the originating PHCC to receive postnatal care (PNC) services. The PHCC continues the care episode in PHENICS within the postnatal framework.

PNC at PHCC Continuity of care
03
PHCC Initiation — Pregnancy Package
How the pregnancy episode is opened in PHENICS

All hospital delivery workflows originate at the PHCC. When a pregnant woman visits and pregnancy is confirmed, the Pregnancy Package is activated in PHENICS to begin tracking the maternal care episode.

⚠
Mandatory field — gestational age
The number of pregnancy weeks (gestational age) is a mandatory field. The Pregnancy Package cannot be activated without this value. Staff must confirm gestational age from clinical assessment before initiating the package.
FieldRequirementNotes
Gestational Age (weeks)MandatoryPackage cannot be activated without this value
Patient ProfileRequiredMust be registered in PHENICS before package activation
PHCC IdentifierSystem-assignedAutomatically linked to the originating PHCC
Pregnancy Package DateSystem-assignedActivation date stamped automatically
04
Antenatal Care (ANC) Visits
Visit requirements and auto-approval restriction rules

Following package activation, the pregnant woman attends ANC visits governed by the restriction manual for auto-approval, which defines the schedule, intervals, and clinical content required at each visit.

✓
Minimum ANC visit threshold
A pregnant woman must complete a minimum of 4 ANC visits at the PHCC to become initially eligible for the delivery service program pool. Patients who have not reached this threshold are not eligible for referral, regardless of their eligibility score.
RequirementValueStatus in PHENICS
Minimum ANC visits for eligibility4 visitsSystem-enforced
Visit schedulingPer auto-approval restriction manualCompliance monitored
Eligibility assessment triggerAfter 4th ANC visitAutomated unlock
05
Eligibility Score & Criteria
Two-part assessment conducted by two separate actors

Eligibility is determined through a structured two-part assessment. Both parts must be completed before PHENICS calculates the composite score.

🩺 PHCC Midwife
  • Medical assessment sections
  • Clinical risk factors
  • Pregnancy health status
  • Obstetric history indicators
🏠 PUI Midwife
  • Socio-economic section
  • Household vulnerability
  • Financial indicators
  • Displacement/residency factors
⚙ PHENICS System
  • Aggregates both sections
  • Calculates composite score
  • Applies threshold rule
  • Unlocks referral if eligible

Composite eligibility score — threshold

Score ≥ 21
010203040+
Score < 21 — Not eligible

Referral is not initiated. Patient remains in ANC management at the PHCC level.

Score ≥ 21 — Eligible

Patient is eligible. PHCC proceeds to initiate a referral via the Delivery Request Act.

ℹ
Sequential dependency
The PUI midwife can only fill the socio-economic section after the PHCC midwife has completed the medical sections. The score is calculated only once both parts are fully submitted. Partial completion does not trigger a score.
06
Hospital Activation Process
Referral initiation, referral form, and hospital-side ID activation

When the eligibility score is ≥ 21, the PHCC initiates a hospital referral through the Delivery Request Act in PHENICS. This generates a referral form that is printed and handed to the pregnant woman.

🔢
Referral ID

Unique identifier for the inter-facility referral transaction. Used to activate the referral record in PHENICS at the hospital level, linking it to the originating PHCC referral.

Found on printed referral form
👤
Patient ID

Unique national identifier for the patient within PHENICS. Used to activate and access the patient profile at the hospital level, enabling delivery recording under the correct episode.

Found on printed referral form
⚠
Both IDs are required
The hospital must activate both the referral (Referral ID) and the patient profile (Patient ID) in PHENICS before any delivery data can be recorded. Attempting to record a delivery without activating both will result in an error or an unlinked episode.
ActionActorPHENICS Step
Initiate referralPHCC staffCreate Delivery Request Act
Print referral formPHCC staffPrint from PHENICS
Present referral form at hospitalPregnant womanPhysical handover
Extract Referral ID & Patient IDHospital staffFrom printed form
Activate referral in PHENICSHospital staffUsing Referral ID
Activate patient profile in PHENICSHospital staffUsing Patient ID
07
Delivery Recording & Discharge
Hospital recording obligations and discharge documentation

Once the referral and patient profile are activated, the hospital records all delivery-related clinical data in PHENICS. The hospital is required to upload a discharge report upon completion of the delivery episode.

Overview
Team composition · 7 members across 3 branches

The Health Information System (HIS) Team operates under the Health Department Management of the Lebanon Mission. The team is responsible for health information strategy, data management, programmatic reporting, and field-level technical support across all health programme areas.

The team is organised into three branches: a Coordination (Central) Office and two field bases — Saida Base and Tripoli Base — each covering a defined geographic catchment of health facilities and programme areas.

Data Flows
End-to-end process flows for HIS Team operational activities
F1
Programmatic Reporting Flow
Monthly data cycle · From data cleaning through final reporting package delivery

The programmatic reporting flow covers the full monthly cycle — from ongoing data cleaning at base level through pivot validation, report production, programme-side validation, and final delivery to the Deputy Health Coordinator. Each stage has a defined responsible actor and escalation path.

📅
Monthly cycle timing
System closure occurs on the second working day of the month. MOPH pivot generation typically occurs the day after closure. All post-closure data cleaning issues must be reported by email to the HIS TM with HIMS and Health Coordinator copied.
HIS Officers — Bases

Ongoing Data Cleaning

Throughout the month, base HIS Officers perform continuous data cleaning within their respective coverage areas. All identified but unresolved issues are documented and reported to the HIS TM on a weekly basis.

Weekly reporting During month
HIS Officers — Coordination

Bi-Weekly Second-Layer Data Verification

Coordination Office HIS Officers perform bi-weekly second-layer verification of data submitted by base offices. Data quality issues identified are flagged directly to the relevant base HIS Officers for cleaning, with findings reported to the HIS TM.

Second-layer verification Reports to HIS TM
System

System Closure

The system is closed on the second working day of the month. Any data cleaning issues identified after closure must be reported immediately to the HIS TM by email, with the HIMS and Health Coordinator copied.

2nd working day Email: HIS TM cc HIMS & Health Coord.
MOPH

Pivot Generation

MOPH generates the data pivot tables, typically on the day following system closure. These pivots are the basis for all programmatic KPI reporting.

Typically day after closure
HIS Team Manager

First Pivot Validation

The HIS TM performs the primary review of the MOPH-generated pivot, checking for missing parameters and data integrity issues. If issues are found, the HIS TM contacts the MOPH consultant directly to request a corrected pivot.

Primary validation MOPH consultant follow-up if needed
HIS Officers — Coordination

Second Pivot Validation

After the HIS TM’s initial review, Coordination HIS Officers conduct a second-level validation of the pivot against internal SOPs and donor-reported KPIs. Any identified discrepancies are reported directly to the HIS TM, who follows up with the MOPH consultant and obtains a corrected pivot if required.

Second-level validation SOP alignment & KPI check
HIS Officers — Coordination

Report Finalisation

Once pivots are validated, Coordination HIS Officers complete and finalise all programmatic reports using the validated pivot data, then submit the reporting package to the HIS TM.

Submit to HIS TM
HIS Team Manager

Report Validation & Sharing with DPMs

The HIS TM reviews and validates the final reporting package, then shares it with the Deputy Programme Managers (DPMs) at the bases for programme-side logical review.

HIS TM validation Distributed to DPMs
Deputy Programme Managers (DPMs)

Programme-Side Validation

DPMs at each base review the reporting figures for logical coherence from the programme perspective. Any discrepancies or concerns are communicated directly to the HIS TM. Upon satisfactory review, the DPM sends an official confirmation email validating the package from the programme side.

Logical validation Official email confirmation
HIS Team Manager

Reporting Package Delivery to DHC

Following DPM validation, the HIS TM sends the finalised reporting package to the Deputy Health Coordinator (DHC) by email. Any issues raised by the DHC are directed back to the HIS TM, with the HIMS copied into the communication loop.

Email to DHC HIMS looped for issues
Deputy Health Coordinator

Reporting Cycle Complete

The reporting package is received and reviewed by the DHC. The monthly programmatic reporting cycle is closed. Any issues raised are escalated through the HIS TM, looping in the HIMS as required.
